objetivo.en: Open and close a written complaint with the formulas of formal correspondence: por medio de la presente and sin otro particular.

traduccion.en: the monthly bill

nota.en: Say “reh-SEE-boh mehn-SWAHL”: c before i sounds like an s. It is the bill a company sends you every month for a service.

traduccion.en: the double charge

nota.en: Say “KOH-broh doo-plee-KAH-doh”: the d between vowels is soft, close to the th in “this”. Un cobro duplicado is a charge made twice for the same thing.

traduccion.en: the subscriber (the customer who holds a phone or internet service)

nota.en: Say “ah-boh-NAH-doh”. The feminine is la abonada. It names the customer of a service company.

traduccion.en: the letterhead

nota.en: Say “mehm-BREH-teh”. The membrete is the name and data of the company printed at the top of a letter.

traduccion.en: the subject line

nota.en: Say “LEE-neh-ah deh ah-SOON-toh”. In an email it is the line that says what the message is about: Asunto: Reclamación por cobro duplicado.

traduccion.en: the treatment received (how the staff treated you)

nota.en: Say “TRAH-toh reh-see-BEE-doh”. Recibido is a participle that agrees with trato: masculine singular.

traduccion.en: the courteous closing

nota.en: Say “SYEH-rreh kohr-TEHS”: the rr in cierre is trilled. Cortés has one form for both genders: un cierre cortés, una frase cortés.

traduccion.en: the provider (the company that gives you a service)

nota.en: Say “prehs-tah-DOHR”: the stress falls on the last syllable. Un prestador de servicios is a company that provides a service, such as internet.

traduccion.en: the written reply

nota.en: Say “kohn-tehs-tah-SYOHN ehs-KREE-tah”. Contestación is a formal word for respuesta; escrita means in writing.

traduccion.en: by means of this letter

nota.en: Say “pohr MEH-dyoh deh lah preh-SEHN-teh”. La presente is short for la presente carta (this letter), so the phrase opens a letter or an email.

traduccion.en: with nothing further to add

nota.en: Say “seen OH-troh pahr-tee-koo-LAHR”. It is a fixed closing formula: you have no other matter to bring up.

explicacion.en: English “Dear” suggests querido, but querido is affectionate, like “my dear”. A formal letter to a company opens with Estimados señores or Estimados señores y señoras. Querido is also masculine singular and señores is plural.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Te escribo para presentar una reclamación.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: Me dirijo a ustedes para presentar una reclamación.

explicacion.en: In English “I am writing to you” works for everyone. In Spanish a company is addressed as ustedes, and a formal letter uses me dirijo a ustedes instead of the colloquial te escribo.

erroresFrecuentes.correcto: Quedo a la espera de su respuesta.

explicacion.en: In English “waiting for” has a preposition, so learners add para. In Spanish esperar takes its object directly, and the formal formula is quedo a la espera de + noun.

titulo.en: The shape of a formal complaint

texto.en: A formal complaint to a company has a fixed shape. At the top, a letter has a membrete (the company's letterhead); an email has a línea de asunto (the subject line): «Asunto: Reclamación por cobro duplicado». Then comes the greeting («Estimados señores:»), the opening formula, the facts, your request, the closing formula and the sign-off. You write to a company in the plural, ustedes, with complete sentences and no colloquial words: no oye, no hola, no ¡qué abuso!. A complaint can be firm, but it must stay courteous. This is the register of the DELE C1 formal letter.

titulo.en: Three formulas to learn as blocks

texto.en: Opening: «Por medio de la presente, me dirijo a ustedes para presentar una reclamación…». La presente means this letter, so the phrase says “by means of this letter”. Closing: «Sin otro particular, quedo a la espera de su respuesta.», literally “with nothing further to add, I remain awaiting your reply”. Sign-off: «Atentamente,» followed by your name, or «Reciba un cordial saludo» for one person and «Reciban un cordial saludo» for a company. Learn each one as a single block: you do not build them word by word. Notice that «Estimados señores:» is not “Dear” in the sense of querido: querido is affectionate, while estimado is for formal letters.

contexto.en: Thursday, May 5, 2033. Emma has found a double charge on her internet bill and phones the customer service of her company; the Agente treats her as usted and she does the same. That night, after her DELE C1 class, Martina comes to Emma's apartment in Guápulo. Emma and Martina use tú, but Martina speaks with the voseo of Argentina. Together they write Emma's first formal email of complaint.

dialogo.texto: Hoy es jueves 5 de mayo y estoy muy molesta, pero voy a mantener la calma. Esta mañana revisé el recibo mensual de mi compañía de internet y encontré un error: en la factura de mayo me cobraron dos veces el plan. Es un cobro duplicado. A las cuatro de la tarde, antes de mi clase del DELE, llamé al servicio al cliente.

traduccion.en: Today is Thursday, May 5, and I am very upset, but I am going to stay calm. This morning I checked the monthly bill from my internet company and I found a mistake: on the May invoice they charged me twice for the plan. It is a double charge. At four in the afternoon, before my DELE class, I called customer service.

dialogo.texto: ¿Cuándo me van a devolver el dinero? ¿Me pueden dar una confirmación por escrito?

traduccion.en: When are you going to return the money to me? Can you give me a confirmation in writing?

traduccion.en: By phone I cannot give you a date or a confirmation in writing. I am going to review your case, Ms. García. That is all I can do today.

dialogo.texto: Entonces les voy a escribir un correo. Muchas gracias.

traduccion.en: Then I am going to write you an email. Thank you very much.

dialogo.texto: Buenas tardes, señora García.

traduccion.en: Good afternoon, Ms. García.

dialogo.texto: Cuando terminó la llamada, yo estaba igual que antes: la Agente me prometió revisar el caso, pero no hizo nada más. Esa noche, después de la clase, Martina vino a mi departamento. Ella es de Buenos Aires: nos tuteamos, pero ella usa el voseo. Le conté todo.

That night, after class, Martina came to my apartment. She is from Buenos Aires: we use tú with each other, but she uses the voseo. I told her everything.

dialogo.texto: Mirá, vos tenés que dejarlo por escrito. Y esto es perfecto para practicar la carta formal del DELE. ¿Querés que te ayude?

traduccion.en: Look, you have to put it in writing. And this is perfect for practicing the formal letter of the DELE. Do you want me to help you?

traduccion.en: Yes, please. I do not want to write the way I talk.

dialogo.texto: Entonces vamos por partes. Primero, la línea de asunto: «Reclamación por cobro duplicado en el recibo mensual de mayo». Después el saludo: «Estimados señores». La apertura es una fórmula, siempre igual: «Por medio de la presente, me dirijo a ustedes para presentar una reclamación». La presente es esta carta.

traduccion.en: Then let's go step by step. traduccion.en: No, querida is for a friend or for the family. For a company you write “Estimados señores,” as I told you. It is a very common mistake among people who study Spanish.

Les agradecería que revisaran el caso y me devolvieran el importe duplicado. Les pido una contestación escrita. Sin otro particular, quedo a la espera de su respuesta. Atentamente, Emma García».

titulo.en: I reiterate my request

objetivo.en: Insist politely on a request that was already sent: recall the date of the first message and set a deadline.

traduccion.en: to reiterate, to repeat a request or statement (formal)

nota.en: Say “reh-ee-teh-RAHR”: four syllables, with the stress on the last one. Reitero mi solicitud = I reiterate my request.

traduccion.en: to date, up to now

nota.en: Say “AHS-tah lah FEH-chah”: the h is silent and ch is as in “cheese”. It goes with the present perfect: Hasta la fecha no he recibido respuesta.

nota.en: Say “ah-VEE-soh reh-ee-teh-RAH-doh”: v sounds like b. A message that repeats an earlier one.

traduccion.en: the pending procedure (a request still open)

nota.en: Say “TRAH-mee-teh pehn-DYEHN-teh”. A trámite is an administrative step; pendiente means it is not finished yet.

traduccion.en: the case number

nota.en: Say “NOO-meh-roh deh KAH-soh”: the r in número is one quick tap, like the tt in American “butter”. It is the reference of your file.

traduccion.en: the unjustified delay

nota.en: Say “reh-TRAH-soh een-hoos-tee-fee-KAH-doh”: j sounds like a strong h. Injustificado means without a good reason.

nota.en: Say “ahm-plyah-SYOHN deh PLAH-soh”: z and ci both sound like an s. Ampliar means to make bigger.

nota.en: Say “FAHL-tah deh rehs-PWEHS-tah”. Falta de + noun means the absence of something.

nota.en: Say “koh-RREH-oh ahn-teh-RYOHR”: the rr in correo is trilled. Anterior means the one before.

nota.en: Say “DEE-ah deh behn-see-MYEHN-toh”: v sounds like b and ci like s. It is the last day to answer.

nota.en: Say “PLAH-soh MAHK-see-moh”: the stress falls on the first syllable of máximo.

explicacion.en: English puts the month first (“May 5”). Spanish gives the day first: el 5 de mayo, and after de the article joins it: del 5 de mayo.

explicacion.en: “Business days” translates word by word into días de negocios, but Spanish says días hábiles, usually inside en un plazo máximo de.

titulo.en: Why a second message?

texto.en: When a company does not answer, a second message must do four things: it says clearly that it repeats an earlier request (reiterar), it recalls the date of the first message, it states that there is still no answer, and it fixes a deadline. The tone stays courteous: the firmness comes from the facts and the dates, not from angry words. The verb is reiterar: «Reitero mi solicitud del 5 de mayo.» A very formal softener is me permito + infinitive, “I take the liberty of”: «Me permito reiterarles mi solicitud.» The pronoun les goes on the infinitive because you are addressing the company.

titulo.en: Tenses, dates and deadlines

texto.en: Two tenses work together. For the first message, a finished moment with a date, use the preterite: «Como ya indiqué en mi correo anterior…» or «Según lo expuesto en mi mensaje del 5 de mayo…». For the silence that continues until now, use the present perfect: «Hasta la fecha no he recibido ninguna respuesta.» Dates follow the pattern el + number + de + month; after a preposition, de + el becomes del: «mi solicitud del 5 de mayo». The deadline is «en un plazo máximo de cinco días hábiles». Días hábiles are working days, so weekends and holidays do not count. English says “five business days”, but Spanish does not say días de negocios.

I ask you to resolve the case within a maximum of five business days; the due date is Monday, May 23. With nothing further to add, I remain awaiting your reply. Sincerely, Emma García.”

titulo.en: I will be forced to turn to

objetivo.en: Escalate a problem firmly and politely, announcing the consequence with me veré obligado/a a + infinitive.

traduccion.en: I will be forced to (literally: I will see myself obliged to)

nota.en: Say “meh veh-REH oh-blee-GAH-doh ah”: veré is the future of ver, with the stress on the last syllable. A woman says me veré obligada a.

traduccion.en: the formal complaint

nota.en: Say “KEH-hah fohr-MAHL”: qu sounds like k and j like a strong h. It is a complaint written for the company or an authority.

traduccion.en: the oversight body, the regulator

nota.en: Say “ohr-gah-NEES-moh deh kohn-TROHL”. A public body that supervises companies, such as banks or phone companies.

traduccion.en: the authority

nota.en: Say “ow-toh-ree-DAHD”: au sounds like “ow” in “cow” and the final d is soft, close to the th in “this”.

traduccion.en: the lawyer

nota.en: Say “ah-boh-GAH-doh”: the g between vowels is soft. The feminine is la abogada.

traduccion.en: the monetary compensation

nota.en: Say “reh-sahr-see-MYEHN-toh peh-koo-NYAH-ryoh”: c before i sounds like an s. Pecuniario is a very formal word for “in money”.

traduccion.en: the legal route

nota.en: Say “VEE-ah leh-GAHL”: v sounds like b and the g in legal is a hard g, as in “go”. Acudir a la vía legal means to go to court or to a lawyer.

traduccion.en: the power, the legal authority to decide

nota.en: Say “poh-tehs-TAHD”: the final d is soft. It is a formal word: the organismo de control has the potestad to fine companies.

traduccion.en: the management (the office of the managers)

nota.en: Say “heh-REHN-syah”: ge sounds like a strong h. You write to la gerencia when the staff cannot solve your problem.

traduccion.en: the failure to comply (with a rule or a deadline)

nota.en: Say “een-ohb-sehr-BAHN-syah”. It is formal: la inobservancia del plazo means they did not respect the deadline.

traduccion.en: the Ombudsman's Office (a public institution that protects people's rights)

nota.en: Say “deh-fehn-soh-REE-ah dehl PWEH-bloh”: the stress falls on the í. In Ecuador it is the public institution that protects people's rights.

traduccion.en: to turn to, to go to (an authority, a lawyer)

nota.en: Say “ah-koo-DEER ah”: the stress falls on the last syllable. Acudir a la autoridad = to turn to the authority.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Seré obligada a acudir a la autoridad.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: Me veré obligada a acudir a la autoridad.

explicacion.en: English says “I will be forced”, so learners use ser + participle. Spanish uses the reflexive verb verse (ver + se, “to see oneself”) + obligado/a: me veré obligada a + infinitive.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Me veré obligado a presentar una denuncia.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: Me veré obligada a presentar una denuncia.

explicacion.en: When a woman writes this, obligado is wrong. English “forced” never changes, so learners keep the masculine. In Spanish obligado/a agrees with the speaker: a woman says obligada.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: A menos que recibo una respuesta, acudiré a la autoridad.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: A menos que reciba una respuesta, acudiré a la autoridad.

explicacion.en: After a menos que (unless) Spanish needs the subjunctive: reciba. English “unless I receive” has no special form, so learners use the indicative.

titulo.en: Escalating with firmness and courtesy

texto.en: When a company ignores two messages, the third step is to announce a consequence. A good escalation has three parts: the facts, the deadline and the consequence. You do not insult and you do not shout in writing: firmness comes from precision. The key structure is «me veré obligado/a a + infinitive». It literally says “I will see myself obliged to…”: the speaker presents the consequence as something the other side forces, not as a personal wish. It is the future of the reflexive verb verse (ver + se, “to see oneself”), and obligado agrees with the speaker: a woman writes «Me veré obligada a acudir a la Defensoría del Pueblo».

titulo.en: Conditions and other formulas

texto.en: To state the condition you can use «de no recibir respuesta, …» (de + infinitive, the same as si no recibo respuesta, but more formal), «en caso contrario, …» (otherwise) or «a menos que + subjunctive» (unless): «A menos que reciba el reembolso, acudiré a la autoridad». Two other formulas express the same idea: «me veré en la necesidad de + infinitive» and «no tendré más remedio que + infinitive». All of them keep the register formal: usted or ustedes, complete sentences, no threats against people.

titulo.en: The verb verse in the future: me veré obligado/a

texto.en: The pronoun and the ending change with the subject, and obligado/a agrees with the person. There is no vosotros form here.

titulo.en: Closing a case: dar por + participle

texto.en: To close a case in writing you can declare how you consider it: «Doy por resuelto el problema» means “I consider the problem solved”. The structure is dar por + participle + the thing: «damos por recibida su carta» (we consider your letter received), «damos por cerrados los trámites» (we consider the procedures closed). It is a formal act: with these words you accept the solution and the case is over. You can also put the object before por: «Doy el caso por resuelto». The impersonal version is also common in official texts: «Se da por concluido el proceso».

titulo.en: The participle agrees with the object

texto.en: The participle works as an adjective of the object, so it agrees in gender and number: resuelto, resuelta, resueltos, resueltas. «Doy por resuelto el problema» (masculine), «doy por resuelta la queja» (feminine), «damos por cerrados los trámites» (masculine plural), «damos por cerradas las reclamaciones» (feminine plural). English participles never change, so this agreement is the hardest part for English speakers. Two fixed expressions look similar: dar por sentado and dar por hecho mean “to take for granted”. Followed by que + a clause, they stay fixed (sentado, hecho): «Doy por hecho que el técnico vendrá mañana» (indicative) and «No doy por sentado que el técnico venga mañana» (subjunctive, because you do not assume it). You already know the absolute participle: «Hecho el pago, se cerró el caso».

contexto.en: Friday, May 27, 2033. After several weeks, the building's new administrator (la Administradora) has the repair done on the leak in the ceiling of Emma's apartment in Guápulo and apologizes for the delay; they use usted with each other. Agradezco también el resarcimiento. Sin otro particular, reciba un cordial saludo. Atentamente, Emma García».

traduccion.en: Yes. I want to say thank you and make everything clear. Here it is: “Subject: Closing of the complaint about the leak. Dear Administradora: By means of this letter, I thank you for the repair of the leak in my apartment and for your visit today. I consider the problem resolved and I consider the complaint closed. I also appreciate the compensation. With nothing further to add, receive a cordial greeting. Sincerely, Emma García.”

dialogo.texto: Perfecto: dos veces «dar por» y cada participio tiene el género correcto: resuelto va con problema y cerrada va con reclamación. Una pregunta: ¿cuál es la diferencia entre dar por resuelto y dar por sentado?

traduccion.en: Perfect: two times “dar por” and each participle has the right gender: resuelto goes with problema and cerrada goes with reclamación. A question: what is the difference between dar por resuelto and dar por sentado?

dialogo.texto: Dar por resuelto es decir que el caso ya terminó. Dar por sentado es suponer algo sin comprobarlo. Yo no doy por sentado que el techo siga seco: mañana lo voy a revisar otra vez. Cerrar un caso por escrito me da tranquilidad: cuando todo queda en un correo, no hay dudas. Gracias, Martina. Y ahora, hecho el papeleo, ¡a estudiar para el DELE!

traduccion.en: Dar por resuelto means saying that the case is already over. Dar por sentado means assuming something without checking it. I do not take for granted that the ceiling will stay dry: tomorrow I am going to check it again. Closing a case in writing gives me peace of mind: when everything is in an email, there are no doubts. Thank you, Martina. And now, the paperwork done, let's study for the DELE!

titulo.en: Two gerunds that formal Spanish avoids

texto.en: The Spanish gerund (-ando / -iendo) is not the same as the English -ing form, and in a formal email two uses are considered mistakes. First, the gerund of posteriority: the gerund shows an action that happens after the main one. «El tren salió, llegando a las ocho» is wrong because arriving comes after leaving; the correct sentence uses y and a conjugated verb: «El tren salió y llegó a las ocho». Second, the adjectival gerund: the gerund describes a noun. «Una caja conteniendo libros» is wrong; Spanish uses a clause with que: «una caja que contiene libros». Both sentences are normal in English (“the train left, arriving at eight”, “a box containing books”), which is why English speakers write them. They also appear in print in Spanish, but careful writing treats them as errors. A few fixed expressions, such as agua hirviendo, are exceptions.

titulo.en: The gerunds that are correct

texto.en: The gerund is correct when it shows an action at the same time as the main verb, or the manner or the means: «Escribo quejándome del servicio» (I write while complaining about the service), «Lo resolvió trabajando mucho» (he solved it by working a lot), «Lo arregló llamando al técnico» (he fixed it by calling the technician). Quick test: if the second action happens later, use y + a conjugated verb («salió y llegó») or que + a verb («una compensación, que llegó el lunes»). If the gerund describes a noun, use que + a verb. A good reviewer looks for these gerunds when polishing the redacción of a formal text.

texto.en: Do not write the left column in a formal text. Read the right column and notice how y or que replaces the gerund.

contexto.en: Tuesday, May 31, 2033. The building's new administrator (la Administradora) asked Emma for a written summary of the leak case for the building's file. Emma shows the draft of her email to Martina, who acts as her reviewer. They use tú, and Martina speaks with the voseo of Argentina. Martina marks four incorrect gerunds and Emma corrects them with her help.

dialogo.texto: Hoy es martes 31 de mayo. La Administradora del edificio me pidió un resumen escrito del caso de la gotera para el archivo. Escribí una versión preliminar del correo y esta tarde se la enseño a Martina, mi revisora. Quiero una redacción perfecta, porque el correo va a un archivo formal.

traduccion.en: Today is Tuesday, May 31. The building's Administradora asked me for a written summary of the leak case for the file. I wrote a preliminary version of the email and this afternoon I am showing it to Martina, my reviewer. I want a perfect wording, because the email goes into a formal file.

dialogo.texto: Dale, mostrame. Hoy soy tu revisora y voy a marcar los errores con el lápiz rojo.

traduccion.en: Okay, show me. Today I am your reviewer and I am going to mark the errors with the red pencil.

dialogo.texto: Aquí está: «Asunto: Resumen del caso de la gotera. Estimada Administradora: Por medio de la presente, le envío un documento adjuntando la factura de la reparación. El técnico vino el lunes, arreglando todo el martes. Pedí una compensación, llegando el lunes. Adjunto también una carta conteniendo la queja. Sin otro particular, reciba un cordial saludo. Atentamente, Emma García».

traduccion.en: Here it is: “Subject: Summary of the leak case. Dear Administradora: By means of this letter, I send you a document attaching the invoice for the repair. The technician came on Monday, fixing everything on Tuesday. I asked for compensation, arriving on Monday. I also attach a letter containing the complaint. With nothing further to add, receive a cordial greeting. Sincerely, Emma García.”

dialogo.texto: El correo es claro y cortés, pero tiene cuatro gerundios incorrectos. Fijate en el primero: «un documento adjuntando la factura». Un gerundio no puede describir un sustantivo. Hay que escribir «un documento que adjunta la factura».

traduccion.en: The email is clear and courteous, but it has four incorrect gerunds. Notice the first one: “un documento adjuntando la factura.” A gerund cannot describe a noun. You have to write “un documento que adjunta la factura.”

dialogo.texto: ¿Por qué no puedo usar el gerundio aquí? En inglés es normal.

traduccion.en: Why can't I use the gerund here? In English it is normal.

dialogo.texto: Porque en español el gerundio tiene reglas. Con un sustantivo usamos una subordinada con «que». Es el mismo problema de «una carta conteniendo la queja»: lo correcto es «una carta que contiene la queja».

traduccion.en: Because in Spanish the gerund has rules. With a noun we use a subordinate clause with “que.” It is the same problem as “una carta conteniendo la queja”: the correct form is “una carta que contiene la queja.”

dialogo.texto: Entiendo. Y la segunda: «El técnico vino el lunes, arreglando todo el martes».

traduccion.en: I understand. And the second one: “El técnico vino el lunes, arreglando todo el martes.”

dialogo.texto: Ahí el gerundio muestra algo que pasa después: primero vino y después arregló. El gerundio normal pasa al mismo tiempo o dice cómo se hace algo, por ejemplo: «lo arregló llamando al técnico». Para dos cosas, una después de otra, se usa «y» y un verbo conjugado: «El técnico vino el lunes y arregló todo el martes».

traduccion.en: There the gerund shows something that happens later: first he came and then he fixed it. The normal gerund happens at the same time or says how something is done, for example: “lo arregló llamando al técnico.” For two things, one after the other, you use “y” and a conjugated verb: “El técnico vino el lunes y arregló todo el martes.”

dialogo.texto: ¿Y «Pedí una compensación, llegando el lunes»?

traduccion.en: And “Pedí una compensación, llegando el lunes”?

dialogo.texto: Es lo mismo: la compensación llegó después de tu pedido. Escribí «Pedí una compensación, que llegó el lunes».

traduccion.en: It is the same: the compensation arrived after your request. Write “Pedí una compensación, que llegó el lunes.”

dialogo.texto: Corregí las cuatro oraciones. Ahora el texto tiene mejor cohesión y más concisión: menos palabras y más orden.

traduccion.en: I corrected the four sentences. Now the text has better cohesion and more conciseness: fewer words and more order.

dialogo.texto: ¡Esa es la depuración! Una buena redacción no necesita palabras largas. Leelo otra vez.

traduccion.en: That is the refining! A good piece of writing does not need long words. Read it again.

dialogo.texto: Tengo otra duda: ¿nunca se puede usar el gerundio en un correo formal?

traduccion.en: I have another question: can the gerund never be used in a formal email?

dialogo.texto: Claro que sí se puede, pero para el modo o para dos cosas que pasan juntas. Por ejemplo, «Les escribo quejándome del cobro» es correcto, porque escribo y me quejo al mismo tiempo. Y «Lo resolvió trabajando mucho» también, porque dice cómo lo resolvió.

traduccion.en: Of course it can, but for the manner or for two things that happen together. For example, “Les escribo quejándome del cobro” is correct, because I write and I complain at the same time. And “Lo resolvió trabajando mucho” too, because it says how he solved it.

dialogo.texto: Aquí está la versión final: «Le envío un documento que adjunta la factura de la reparación. El técnico vino el lunes y arregló todo el martes. Pedí una compensación, que llegó el lunes. Adjunto también una carta que contiene la queja».

traduccion.en: Here is the final version: “I send you a document that attaches the invoice for the repair. The technician came on Monday and fixed everything on Tuesday. I asked for compensation, which arrived on Monday. I also attach a letter that contains the complaint.”

dialogo.texto: Perfecto. Un revisor nunca da por sentado que un texto esté bien: lo lee dos veces. Ahora sí, mandalo.

traduccion.en: Perfect. A reviewer never takes for granted that a text is good: he reads it twice. Now yes, send it.

dialogo.texto: Gracias, Martina. Lo envío hoy mismo, y así termino mayo con tres reclamaciones bien escritas.

traduccion.en: Thank you, Martina. I am sending it today, and that way I end May with three well-written complaints.

consigna.en: (Open) Write at least 30 words in Spanish: rewrite these four sentences without the incorrect gerund, using y + verb or que + verb: 1. Envié una carta conteniendo mi queja. 2. El técnico vino el lunes, arreglando la gotera el martes. 3. Adjunto un documento mostrando la factura. 4. Salimos del banco, llegando a casa a las seis.

feedback.en: Model: 1 and 3 become que + verb (que contiene, que muestra); 2 and 4 become y + a conjugated verb (y arregló, y llegamos).
